name: Mission of Burma
label: Matador
lede: Mission of Burma lasted four years the first time, put out one EP and one album, and ended when Roger Miller's ears gave out. Nineteen years later the Boston band everyone had been covering came back and made four more records as loud as the first.

eras.title: Sun Ra auditions, and a plaque on a door
eras.text: After Moving Parts split, Roger Miller and Clint Conley built a four-piece in which the fourth member played tape machines instead of an instrument. Boston college radio got there first.

years.h: Miller and Conley audition drummers with Sun Ra and James Brown
years.p: After Moving Parts splits amicably, Roger Miller and Clint Conley play 'out' music at drummer auditions until each applicant gives up and leaves.
years.xp: The name came from a plaque Conley saw on a diplomatic building in New York reading Mission of Burma. He liked that it sounded, in the article's words, "murky and disturbing".

years.big: crossing John Coltrane with the Ramones
years.h: Mission of Burma debuts as a trio at the Modern Theater
years.p: Peter Prescott's own description of the band, on drums for the first show in Boston. Sets were put together by committee minutes before going on.
years.xp:
Prescott, formerly of the Molls, was the third member that night. The fourth, Martin Swope, hadn't arrived yet.

Boston critic Tristram Lozaw said the shows swung between spectacular and a ball of incomprehensible noise, and nobody, the band included, knew which they'd get.

years.h: Swope joins, with a pile of tape machines
years.p: Miller writes Nu Disco and calls Martin Swope for tape loops. Swope runs live sound and feeds sped-up, slowed and reversed tape of the band back through the PA.

years.h: WMBR plays Peking Spring until it tops the year
years.p: MIT's station makes Conley's song its most-played of 1979. By the time a label turned up, the band felt it had run its course.

years.h: The band hates the clean sound on its first single
years.p: Academy Fight Song, with Miller's Max Ernst on the other side, is made with Rick Harte producing. Harte's layered mix was far tidier than the band's live noise, and the first pressing sold out anyway.
years.xp: The band objected to the production at first. [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] and Miracle Legion later covered Academy Fight Song.

eras.title: Loud enough to cost Miller his hearing
eras.text: Mission of Burma made one EP and one album for Boston's Ace of Hearts, both now counted among the great American records of the decade. The volume was the point, and Miller paid for it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Signals, Calls, and Marches · Wikipedia: Mission of Burma
yt: Live on WERS FM, Boston, Jan 24, 1981
years.h: Signals, Calls, and Marches sells out 10,000 copies
years.p: The EP, recorded January to March 1981, opens with Conley's That's When I Reach for My Revolver. The first pressing was gone by the end of the year.
years.xp:
Revolver was covered later by [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]], [[Graham Coxon|fb56cc34-2ab1-4621-ac18-9bf2895e5f4f]], [[Catherine Wheel|37e3dd97-73f9-4c69-b50d-0c0e3c47c40c]], [[Pegboy|13e78eec-9ee4-47f2-a50e-2a9f519cb6e2]] and [[Down by Law|7d990fa3-e1a0-4d6e-b266-222a66bd3f83]], among others.

Miller remembered a Cleveland show around 1981 or 1982 where fans who loved the record backed against the wall at live volume and wouldn't clap.
play: That's When I Reach for My Revolver

years.h: Dredd Foole and the Din get the whole band as backing
years.p: Singer Dan Ireton records a two-song single in February with Miller on organ, Conley on lead guitar and Swope on prepared bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Vs. · Wikipedia: Mission of Burma
years.h: Vs. is recorded in Rhode Island in four months
years.p: Made at Normandy Sound from January to April 1982 with Harte, it is the band's only 1980s album. The Boston Phoenix said Trem Two sounded like the universe being born and destroyed.
years.xp: Robert Christgau gave it a B+ in the Village Voice and later said he should have given it an A-. The band [[Versus|ee7db106-6996-42a9-981d-b2d55a9b8366]] took its name from the album.

years.h: Rifle-range earmuffs, and a band that has to stop
years.p: Miller's tinnitus from years of extreme volume reaches a dangerous level. On the farewell tour he plays in rifle-range earmuffs over foam earplugs.
years.xp: The last shows ran through Boston, including the Bradford Hotel and the Channel, plus Chicago, New York and Detroit. They were taped and became The Horrible Truth About Burma, with covers of [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]]' 1970 and [[Pere Ubu|5a54b72e-bfb3-4ca6-944a-e17261399965]]'s Heart of Darkness.

eras.title: Nineteen years of being covered
eras.text: The members scattered into tape-loop art music, new punk bands and a TV newsroom. The records got reissued, the songs got covered, and a generation of bands learned them.

yt: Academy Fight Song, live in Boston, 1983
years.h: The farewell tour goes out as The Horrible Truth About Burma
years.p: Ace of Hearts releases the 1983 recordings in 1985. The title is an inside joke about how chaotic the band's shows could be.

years.h: Miller and Swope go to tape; Prescott starts Volcano Suns
years.p: Roger Miller and Martin Swope work with Erik Lindgren in [[Birdsongs of the Mesozoic|0a3d592f-8848-4ac0-888d-f31eb4be5bfe]]. Peter Prescott forms [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]], later Kustomized and the Peer Group.

years.h: Conley produces Yo La Tengo, then goes to TV news
years.p: Clint Conley produces [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]]'s Ride the Tiger, then earns a broadcast journalism master's and works for years as a producer on WCVB-TV's Chronicle.

years.h: A Mission of Burma CD runs past the 80-minute limit
years.p: Rykodisc's compilation Mission of Burma is the first CD to go over 80 minutes, past the format's supposed ceiling.

years.h: Our Band Could Be Your Life gives Burma a chapter
years.p: [[Michael Azerrad|532857f4-2f6c-4e89-a280-1cdb68c3e6ec]]'s book counts Mission of Burma among 13 bands that built the American underground. Conley is already playing again in a new band, Consonant.

eras.title: Two shows become a second career
eras.text: Conley started playing again, Martin Swope wasn't coming back, and a friend from Peter Prescott's old band took over the tapes. A pair of reunion dates turned into fourteen years.

q: Bob opted for maintaining the original integrity, and uses a tape deck.
years.h: Two reunion shows sell out so fast they become five
years.p: Tickets go so fast the dates grow to three nights in Boston and two in New York. Swope, now in Hawaii, declines; [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s Bob Weston takes over the tapes.
years.xp:
Weston had played in Prescott's [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]]. Miller told him he could use digital gear; Weston stuck with reel-to-reel. He later added an Electro-Harmonix looper live but kept real tape in the studio.

The band had planned only two gigs.

eras.title: Matador, and a day with their name on it
eras.text: Most reunions coast. This one made new albums for Matador Records that critics put next to the old ones, got its catalog reissued, and got October 4 named after it.

years.h: ONoffON ends a 19-year silence
years.p: Matador releases it in May, produced by Bob Weston with Rick Harte. It finishes 90th in the Village Voice Pazz & Jop poll.

years.h: The Obliterati, nearly called Aluminum Washcloth
years.p: Pitchfork ranks the May release 33rd among 2006's records. The documentary Not a Photograph: The Mission of Burma Story comes out the same year.
years.xp: It also placed 50th in the Village Voice Pazz & Jop poll.

years.h: Matador reissues Signals, Vs. and Horrible Truth
years.p: All three 1980s records come back remastered in March. Signals, Calls, and Marches gains two unreleased songs from its first session.

years.h: Prescott tells L.A. Record the band has a couple of years left
years.p: Peter Prescott says the physical demands of a Burma show limit the band to a couple more years at most.
years.xp: The band went on for eight more years after that interview, until the Berlin show in 2016.

years.cap: Mission of Burma Day, MIT, October 4, 2009
years.h: Boston declares October 4 Mission of Burma Day
years.p: The City Council's proclamation is marked at a ceremony at MIT in Cambridge, home of WMBR, which played Peking Spring to death in 1979.

years.h: The Sound the Speed the Light arrives with 14 songs
years.p: A Matador 7-inch of two non-album tracks comes first, in August.

eras.title: Berlin, then a quiet end
eras.text: One more album on a new label, a last show in Berlin, and an amicable end. The returns since have been for a friend.

years.cap: Clint Conley, Beachcomber, Wellfleet, Massachusetts, August 11, 2012
years.h: Unsound leaves Matador for Fire Records
years.p: Mission of Burma parts ways with Matador and makes its fifth album for Fire Records, with Dust Devil as the single.

years.h: Berlin turns out to be the last gig of the reunion
years.p: The band plays Berlin in 2016. It is the last show of the reunion era.

years.h: WBUR reports that Mission of Burma has split, and it's friendly
years.p: A 2019 Facebook post had said no more albums. In June 2020 WBUR reports that Conley, Miller and Prescott remain good friends.

yt: Fan-shot clip, Middle East Downstairs, Mar 12, 2026
years.h: A benefit for Jeff Conolly, Clint Conley's friend since Darien
years.p: Mission of Burma plays the Middle East Downstairs in Cambridge for [[Lyres|f15227ba-75e0-490c-a817-63bf8f54fee7]] leader Jeff Conolly. A second benefit follows at Brighton Music Hall on August 14.
